_comment: The run matrix, tiered so the budget goes where the claims are. Expand it with
uv run python experiments/common/run_spec.py experiments/configs/matrix.json data/chimera_coco/manifest.json
A full factorial (2 models x 2 regimes x 4 pairs x 5 counts x 3 seeds x 6 attacks) is ~1000 runs and does
not fit the compute budget; these tiers keep 3 seeds where a confidence interval is claimed and 1 seed
where the point is a trend or a generalisation check.
eval_guidance is read by the evaluation step: the full omega sweep only where the paper plots it.
steps is pinned to 800 (one epoch over the 3200-image clean corpus at batch 1 x accum 4) rather than
left to epochs: derived from epochs it would grow with poison_count (3400 images -> 850 steps), so a
poison-count sweep would vary training length as well as poison count.

full_ft.source: results/compute/full_ft_probe_l4.json (Modal L4, 512px); price $0.000222/s = $0.799/h (modal.com/pricing, checked 2026-10-27), CPU+memory billed on top

tiers.name: clean_baseline
tiers._why: B0: fine-tuning on a clean corpus must leave attack success at ~0. The check the old H1 failed.

tiers.name: headline_curve
tiers._why: Fig. 'ASR vs number of poisons' on both architectures: the H1 result and the H2 result in one grid.

tiers.name: generalisation
tiers._why: Does the result hold on the other three concept pairs? One count, one seed, strongest baseline only.

tiers.name: lora
tiers._why: Secondary regime: how most SD3 fine-tunes are actually made. Fits the free Kaggle T4.
